This is consistent with the PA requirement contributing to the decline, but pre/post evidence is an association and cannot prove causation.

arguments.summary: Eastvale's GLP-1 prior authorization requirement took effect 2024-07-01, and GLP-1 prescribing fell 18.6% (95% CI −20.8% to −16.2%) comparing the four final quarters before vs after — a statistically significant and material change [E1][E3]. The timing is sharp: GLP-1 scripts per 1,000 member-months were flat at 11.8–12.5 through 2024Q2, then dropped to 9.79 in 2024Q3, a −21.4% quarter-over-quarter step [E5][E6]. SGLT2, which was not subject to this PA, stayed flat over the same period, which argues the drop is GLP-1-specific rather than a system-wide artifact [E7]. This is consistent with the PA requirement contributing to the decline, but pre/post evidence is an association and cannot prove causation.

findings.statement: EV's GLP-1 PA requirement is effective 2024-07-01 per the provider manual EV-MAN-2024-PH; an earlier bulletin date of 2024-06-01 (EV-BUL-2024-007) was superseded by EV-BUL-2024-011, which postponed the start so prescribers could prepare documentation [E1][E4].
The PA criteria: (1) type 2 diabetes with A1c >= 7.0 after a metformin trial, or (2) BMI >= 35 with a documented weight-related comorbidity; approvals last 12 months [EV-MAN-2024-PH#p1].

GLP-1 prescriptions per 1,000 member-months fell from a pre-period mean of 12.094 to 9.846 post-period, a −18.6% change (95% CI −20.8% to −16.2%), verdict significant_and_material at a 5% threshold [E3].

The quarterly series shows a level shift exactly at the policy start: 2024Q1 11.96 and 2024Q2 12.45, then 2024Q3 9.79, 2024Q4 10.05, 2025Q1 9.57, 2025Q2 9.97, against a pre-policy range of 11.75–12.45 [E5].
The 2024Q2→2024Q3 drop was −21.4%, showing most of the change occurred as a step at the effective date rather than a pre-existing downward trend [E5][E6].
SGLT2 prescribing in EV (not subject to the GLP-1 PA) stayed roughly flat at 14.7–15.7 per 1,000 member-months from 2023Q1 through 2025Q2, so the GLP-1 decline is drug-class specific [E7].

arguments.confidence_reason: Timing alignment, magnitude, and drug-class specificity all point to the PA requirement as a plausible driver, and the pre/post result is significant with a CI excluding zero. But pre/post comparison is an association only; there is no control-state or interrupted time-series design, only 4 pre and 4 post quarters, and 8 suppressed rows fall in the analysis window.
caveats: Pre/post differences are associations, not proof the PA requirement caused the decline; other concurrent factors (formulary changes, utilization management, market shifts) were not evaluated.
